intro.title: useSyncExternalStore
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular component that displays a real-time counter, learning how to integrate external state into Angular's reactive system. You'll use the useSyncExternalStore pattern, a concept for subscribing to and synchronizing with external data sources like browser APIs or third-party libraries. The main technologies involved are Angular components, TypeScript, and RxJS Observables to handle the subscription logic. By the end, you'll understand how to keep your UI in sync with external state changes efficiently and reactively.
intro.usecase: In real Angular applications, useSyncExternalStore is essential for synchronizing UI components with external data sources like WebSocket connections, browser APIs, or third-party libraries. You'll see this pattern in live dashboards that display real-time stock prices or IoT sensor data, where components must react instantly to external updates. It's also used in collaborative tools like shared document editors where cursor positions or user presence indicators update continuously. Developers implement this to ensure their components stay in sync with rapidly changing external state without manual subscription management.
